card: ALIAS: Kioka (possibly — the name Magon creatures invoked after the confrontation; unresolved whether it names this figure or a separate identity)

ROLE: Silver-haired youth or humanoid who pressed to ascend above the mushroom-dome settlement, followed the ape companion into the dangerous upper territory despite warnings, fought through a Magon tribal confrontation, and emerged airborne after defeating a giant creature.
TRAIT: Appears able to float or hover; the mechanism is unconfirmed, with specialized footwear only a possibility.
TRAIT: Equipped with extended metal claws usable in close-quarters combat.
TRAIT: Insistent and driven — pressed the ape companion to lead the way above the mushroom domes despite explicit warnings of danger.
TRAIT: Claims sworn brotherhood with the ape companion; treats this bond as justification for shared risk.
TRAIT: Survived being seized by a giant creature by tearing or blasting through its head area in reversal.

RELATIONSHIP: the-ape-companion (The Ape Companion): sworn brother and companion; Kiowotai pressed him toward the heights using the language of sworn brotherhood; the ape led the way despite warning of the danger.

RELATIONSHIP: Magon people: perceived prophetic figure; after the confrontation Magon creatures invoked Kioka as their master and spoke of departure to the Diamond Planet; the Magon legend of a little white ape was recited during the encounter, but whether this constitutes fulfillment is not confirmed.

VOICE: Speaks with direct insistence; presses the ape companion into action using the language of sworn brotherhood; resolve expressed through persistence and physical commitment rather than elaborate argument.
BOUNDARY: Kiowotai is a silver-haired humanoid distinct from the ape companion called Aghnar; do not merge those identities unless the story explicitly resolves the uncertainty.
BOUNDARY: A possible connection between Kiowotai and another figure named Aghnar remains unresolved; treat it as an open question, not as a confirmed identification.
BOUNDARY: The Magon invocation of Kioka is possibly another name for this figure but is unresolved; do not treat Kioka and Kiowotai as a confirmed single identity.

BOUNDARY: The Magon legend of a little white ape and the creatures' post-battle invocation suggest possible prophetic recognition; treat this as Magon belief, not as confirmed fulfillment of any prophecy.

manual_review_notes: Source-thin singleton, but the card is format-valid, source-grounded, and appropriately preserves the Kiowotai/Kioka/Aghnar uncertainty instead of importing later or wiki-resolution lore.
